body.div: This class is used as an abstract superclass for expressions where the consuming operand is absorbed by the expression: for example, data(), string(), or copy-of(). It handles the fact that the input can be crawling, which means that selected nodes can be nested. We therefore need to be collecting the result values of multiple nodes during the same pass of the input. Hence we maintain a stack of values-under-construction. Moreover, an inner value will be available before the outer value, but it follows the outer value in document order, so it needs to be held pending until the outer value is available. Hence we maintain a list of values that are ready to be output.

body.div:
A Feed is a processing object that sits on a push pipeline to evaluate some expression. One operand of the expression is a streamed operand, and this operand delivers a sequence either of composed items, or of start/end element events (or a mixture of both). The calls to the Feed represent incremental events in the evaluation of the streamed operand. The Feed is responsible for processing this stream of events and generating a new stream of events representing the result of the expression, which are pushed to the next step in the pipeline in the same way.
A "composed feed" consists entirely of items, supplied using the processItem interface. A "decomposed feed" represents a tree using a sequence of startElement/endElement events. In general the code for a particular expression should be prepared to accept either. However, in many cases (especially expressions that atomize their operand), it is known that the input will always be composed, as a result of the action of an earlier step in the pipeline.
A Feed musy be serially reusable; that is, its state after exiting the close() method must be the same as the state before entering the open() method.

comment.sentence: A Feed is a processing object that sits on a push pipeline to evaluate some expression.
The close() method is called immediately before the Watch is destroyed, that is, when the element whose declaration scopes the constraint implemented by this Watch goes out of scope.

Appends the output of an ItemFeed to a SequenceReceiver.
This works as follows. When the startElement event for a matched node is reported, this feed simply returns a Receiver to the WatchManager. The WatchManager then notifies all events from this startElement to the matching endElement (inclusive) to that Receiver. So all the events for the matched node and its descendants are passed on unchanged.
The Receiver that is actually returned to the WatchManager is the Receiver obtained from the next expression in the push pipeline, but with a simple filter attached that suppresses open() and close() events. Without this, the WatchManager would close the receiver when the endElement event occurs, which is inappropriate when the expression selects a sequence of elements.

This class is used when a streaming template requests evaluation of a simple content constructor in streaming mode (that is, when it constructs a text, attribute, comment, or PI node based on the contents of the streamed document).
The result of this Watch is a single string, constructed using the rules of "Constructing Simple Content" in the XSLT specification.
The AdjacentTextNodeMergerFeed is used when the node is constructed as a result of a computation on the streamed data, for example xsl:value-of select="distinct-values(.//@price)". By contrast, a SimpleContentWatch is used when the streamed nodes are selected directly, for example xsl:value-of select=".//@price".
Both a Feed and a Watch are needed because a simple content constructor operates on a sequence of nodes without simply atomizing the sequence.

The close() method is called immediately before the Watch is destroyed, that is, when the element whose declaration scopes the constraint implemented by this Watch goes out of scope.

comment.sentence: A StringValueAccumulator is a Receiver that computes the string value of an element in streaming mode, by copying all the text nodes to a supplied receiver.
This class is used when a streamed template requests evaluation of the typed value of the nodes selected by a path expression.
